source_title: Candelabrum cells are ubiquitous cerebellar cortex interneurons with specialized circuit properties
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises candelabrum cells as the most abundant Purkinje-layer interneuron, GABAergic and molecularly distinct, using snRNA sequencing and electrophysiology.
summary: Candelabrum cells (CCs) are the most abundant interneuron in the Purkinje cell layer, are GABAergic, molecularly distinct, and present in all cerebellar lobules. Their high input resistance makes firing highly sensitive to synaptic inputs; they are excited by mossy fibers and granule cells and strongly inhibited by Purkinje cells. CCs primarily inhibit molecular layer interneurons, leading to Purkinje cell disinhibition.
quotes: Candelabrum cells (CCs) are enigmatic interneurons of the cerebellar cortex that have been identified based on their morphology, but their electrophysiological properties, synaptic connections and function remain unknown.
We find that CCs are the most abundant PC layer interneuron. They are GABAergic, molecularly distinct and present in all cerebellar lobules.
CCs in turn primarily inhibit molecular layer interneurons, which leads to PC disinhibition.

synonyms_found.quote: Candelabrum cells (CCs) are enigmatic interneurons of the cerebellar cortex

source_title: Candelabrum cells are molecularly distinct, ubiquitous interneurons of the cerebellar cortex with specialized circuit properties
node_relevance_reason: Preprint directly characterising candelabrum cells as GABAergic, molecularly distinct Purkinje-layer interneurons using snRNA sequencing, electrophysiology, and serial EM.
summary: This preprint (earlier version of Osorno et al. 2022) establishes candelabrum cells as the most abundant Purkinje-layer interneuron, GABAergic and molecularly distinct, present in all cerebellar lobules. CCs are excited by mossy fibers/granule cells, inhibited by Purkinje cells, and disinhibit Purkinje cells by inhibiting molecular layer interneurons.
quotes: CCs are the most abundant PC layer interneuron. They are GABAergic, molecularly distinct, and present in all cerebellar lobules.
CCs are excited by MFs and granule cells, and strongly inhibited by PCs. CCs in turn inhibit molecular layer interneurons, which leads to PC disinhibition.

source_title: Morphological pseudotime ordering and fate mapping reveal diversification of cerebellar inhibitory interneurons
node_relevance_reason: Directly addresses MLI1/MLI2 transcriptomic subtypes and confirms that Sorcs3 and Nxph1 distinguish the two MLI transcriptional types, along with Pvalb as a shared marker.
summary: Wang & Lefebvre (2022) combined genetic fate-mapping and pseudotemporal morphological profiling to show that MLIs derive from a common progenitor but diversify into two discrete morphological types with extensive within-class heterogeneity. Transcriptomically, MLI types are distinguished by Sorcs3 or Nxph1 expression (from Kozareva et al. 2021). Basket cells (BCs) populate the lower molecular layer forming perisomatic basket terminals and pinceaux; stellate cells (SCs) integrate into the upper molecular layer targeting Purkinje cell dendritic shafts.
quotes: Differential gene expression analyses confirmed that MLI t-types were distinguished by Sorcs3 or Nxph1 expression51.
Basket cells (BCs) are born earlier, populate the lower third of the molecular layer (ML) and form a series of perisomatic basket terminals that enwrap the cell bodies of Purkinje cells.
MLI1 and MLI2, but surprisingly these transcriptionally-defined subtypes did not obviously correlate with BC or SC features nor with a laminar organization within the molecular layer.

later-born stellate cells (SCs) integrate into the upper molec

source_title: Cerebellar circuits for disinhibition and synchronous inhibition
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises MLI1 and MLI2 subtypes in the molecular layer, showing MLI1s primarily inhibit Purkinje cells (basket/lower-layer identity) and MLI2s disinhibit Purkinje cells by inhibiting MLI1s.
summary: Lackey et al. 2023 (preprint of Lackey et al. 2024 Neuron) demonstrates that MLI1s and MLI2s are functionally specialised: MLI1s are electrically coupled, fire synchronously, and primarily inhibit Purkinje cells (pausing PC firing), while MLI2s are not electrically coupled and primarily inhibit MLI1s to disinhibit Purkinje cells. This circuit supports cerebellar-dependent learning through gated disinhibition.
quotes: MLI1s primarily inhibit PCs, are electrically coupled to each other, fire synchronously with other MLI1s on the millisecond time scale in vivo, and synchronously pause PC firing.
MLI2s are not electrically coupled, they primarily inhibit MLI1s and disinhibit PCs, and are well suited to gating cerebellar-dependent learning8.

source_title: Purkinje cell collaterals preferentially target a subtype of molecular layer interneuron
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises MLI1 and MLI2 connectivity, including PC synapses onto MLI subtypes and candelabrum cell (PLI) synapses preferentially onto MLI1s, with Pvalb-positive MLI identity.
summary: Lackey et al. 2025 shows that Purkinje cell axon collaterals preferentially synapse onto MLI2s (7%) and PLIs/candelabrum cells (32%), with fewer synapses on MLI1s (6%). Candelabrum cells form many more synapses onto MLI1s than MLI2s. The PC-MLI2-MLI1-PC and PC-candelabrum-MLI1-PC pathways allow PC firing to disinhibit MLI1s, providing negative feedback.
quotes: MLI1s primarily inhibit PCs whereas MLI2s mainly inhibit MLI1s and disinhibit PCs.
EM reconstructions show that PCs make 53% of their synapses onto other PCs, 32% onto PLIs, 6% onto MLI1s and 7% onto MLI2s.
candelabrum cells, a type of PLI, form many more synapses onto MLI1s than MLI2s.

source_title: Molecular layer interneurons shape the spike activity of cerebellar Purkinje cells
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises basket cells and stellate cells as GABAergic molecular layer interneurons with distinct functional roles on Purkinje cell firing pattern and rate.
summary: Brown et al. (2019) used genetic silencing of GABAergic output in stellate cells vs. basket cells (via Ascl1-CreER) and found stellate cells establish Purkinje cell simple spike firing pattern while basket cells determine firing rate. Basket cells reside in the basal molecular layer (~55% recombination) and stellate cells in the apical molecular layer (~63% recombination). Both arise from a common progenitor in the ventricular zone.
quotes: stellate cells establish the Purkinje cell simple spike firing pattern whereas basket cells determine their rate.
This study establishes complementary roles for the GABAergic function of cerebellar molecular layer interneurons.

the majority of labeled cells were found in their canonical regions of the molecular layer with ~55% recombination in the basal molecular layer for the basket cell scheme and ~63% recombination in the apical molecular layer for the stellate cell scheme

source_title: Feedback inhibition underlies new computational functions of cerebellar interneurons
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises the four cerebellar inhibitory interneuron types (Golgi, candelabrum, basket, stellate) and their anatomical locations (granule cell layer, Purkinje cell layer, molecular layer), and introduces candelabrum cells.
summary: Halverson et al. (2022) identifies cerebellar inhibitory interneurons including Golgi cells (granule cell layer), candelabrum cells (Purkinje cell layer), and basket and stellate cells (molecular layer). They present evidence that some MLIs in the inner third of the molecular layer receive PC feedback inhibition via glutamate, leading to disinhibition of other PCs.
quotes: Within the cerebellar cortex, Golgi, candelabrum, basket and stellate cells have been identified as inhibitory interneurons (Hull and Regehr, 2022).

basket and stellate cells reside within the molecular layer of the cerebellar cortex. These molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) form inhibitory synapses with each other, as well as with PCs, the only output cells of the cerebellar cortex.

synonyms_found.quote: These molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) form inhibitory synapses with each other

source_title: Microcircuit Rules Governing Impact of Single Interneurons on Purkinje Cell Output In Vivo
node_relevance_reason: Directly studies molecular layer interneurons and their inhibitory impact on Purkinje cells in vivo, characterising how interneuron location shapes functional impact.
summary: Arlt & Häusser (2020) used dual patch-clamp recordings from MLIs and Purkinje cells in vivo to show that single interneuron spikes can potently inhibit Purkinje cell output depending on interneuron location. Climbing fiber input activates many interneurons via glutamate spillover but inhibits interneurons that target the same Purkinje cell receiving the climbing fiber, forming a disinhibitory motif.
quotes: single interneuron spikes can potently inhibit Purkinje cell output, depending on interneuron location.

Climbing fiber input activates many interneurons via glutamate spillover but results in inhibition of those interneurons that inhibit the same Purkinje cell receiving the climbing fiber input, forming a disinhibitory motif.

source_title: Early molecular layer interneuron hyperactivity triggers Purkinje neuron degeneration in SCA1
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises molecular layer interneurons (MLINs) with parvalbumin as a marker and their GABAergic inhibitory role on Purkinje neurons.
summary: Pilotto et al. (2023) found that molecular layer interneurons become prematurely hyperexcitable in SCA1, expressing abnormally elevated parvalbumin (Pvalb) and displaying more numerous synaptic connections onto Purkinje neurons. Chemogenetic inhibition of hyperexcitable MLINs restored calcium signalling in Purkinje neurons and delayed their degeneration.
quotes: Mutant MLINs express abnormally elevated parvalbumin, harbor high excitatory-to-inhibitory synaptic density, and display more numerous synaptic connections on PNs, indicating an excitation/inhibition imbalance.
Chemogenetic inhibition of hyperexcitable MLINs normalizes parvalbumin expression and restores calcium signaling in Sca1 PNs.

synonyms_found.quote: an inhibitory circuit element (molecular layer interneurons [MLINs]) that becomes prematurely hyperexcitable

source_title: Purkinje cell neurotransmission patterns cerebellar basket cells into zonal modules defined by distinct pinceau sizes
section: Cerebellar basket cell interneurons have a complex structural interaction with Purkinje cells
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises cerebellar basket cells and their synaptic specialisation (pinceau) onto Purkinje cells, including their location in the molecular layer and the presence of candelabrum cells in the Purkinje cell layer.
summary: Zhou et al. (2020) demonstrates that basket cells form dense inhibitory plexuses around Purkinje cell somata and axon initial segments (pinceau). Purkinje cell neurotransmission patterns basket cells into zonal modules defined by different pinceau sizes. The Purkinje cell layer also contains candelabrum cells and Bergmann glia alongside Purkinje cells.
quotes: The most superficial layer contains inhibitory interneurons called basket cells and stellate cells, as well as excitatory climbing fibers and parallel fibers (the axons of granule cells). All four cell types project onto the Purkinje cells.
The PCL also contains candelabrum cells and large astrocytes called Bergmann glia.
Staining using a modified version of the Golgi-Cox method reveals the dense axonal projections of the basket cells around Purkinje cells.

synonyms_found.quote: make up the middle cerebellar cortical layer called the Purkinje cell layer (PCL)
synonyms_found.section: Cerebellar basket cell interneurons have a complex structural interaction with Purkinje cells

source_title: Besides Purkinje cells and granule neurons: an appraisal of the cell biology of the interneurons of the cerebellar cortex
node_relevance_reason: Comprehensive review of cerebellar interneurons including candelabrum cells, basket cells, and stellate cells with detailed anatomical descriptions of each type.
summary: Schilling et al. (2008) reviews cerebellar interneuron biology beyond the classic four cell types, highlighting candelabrum cells, Lugaro cells, and unipolar brush cells. Candelabrum cell perikarya are in the Purkinje cell layer with axons projecting into the molecular layer in a horizontal, parasagittal pattern. Basket cells reside in the lower molecular layer targeting Purkinje cell somata; stellate cells project to distal Purkinje cell dendritic shafts.
quotes: Candelabrum cell perikarya are located within the ganglionic (Purkinje) cell layer, and they are usually elongated along the vertical axis.

Basket cells project to the Purkinje cell bodies and the axon initial hillock — actually this is the very prerequisite to define a basket cell. Stellate cells in contrast, project to more distant dendritic shafts.
besides the four neuronal phenotypes just mentioned, the cerebellar cortex contains several other types of neurons, among them candelabrum cells, Lugaro cells, and unipolar brush cells.

source_title: Movement Rate Is Encoded and Influenced by Widespread, Coherent Activity of Cerebellar Molecular Layer Interneurons
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises molecular layer interneurons (basket and stellate cells) as a population whose activity encodes movement rate and influences motor output in the lateral cerebellum.
summary: Gaffield & Christie (2017) used in vivo Ca2+ imaging to show that MLIs in the lateral cerebellum are broadly active during rhythmic motor behaviour (licking), with population activity correlating with movement rate. Chemogenetic suppression of MLI output reduced lick rate, demonstrating an integral role in motor control.
quotes: Inhibition from molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) is thought to play an important role in cerebellar function by sharpening the precision of Purkinje cell spike output.
MLIs were robustly active during lick-related movement across a lobule-specific region of the cerebellum showing high temporal correspondence within their population.
Chemogenetic suppression of MLI output reduced lick rate and altered tongue movements

source_title: Molecular layer interneurons: Key elements of cerebellar network computation and behavior.
node_relevance_reason: Review directly characterising molecular layer interneurons (basket and stellate cells) as key elements controlling Purkinje cell activity via inhibitory synaptic transmission.
summary: Kim & Augustine (2020) review the organization of MLI circuits, covering chemical and electrical synapses that form spatially structured clusters amplifying feedforward and lateral inhibition to shape Purkinje cell activity. Recent in vivo studies confirm MLI circuits contribute to sensorimotor processing, motor coordination, and cognitive processes.
quotes: Molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) play an important role in cerebellar information processing by controlling Purkinje cell (PC) activity via inhibitory synaptic transmission.

A local MLI network, constructed from both chemical and electrical synapses, is organized into spatially structured clusters that amplify feedforward and lateral inhibition to shape the temporal and spatial patterns of PC activity.

source_title: Electrotonic Coupling Interacts with Intrinsic Properties to Generate Synchronized Activity in Cerebellar Networks of Inhibitory Interneurons
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises basket and stellate cells as the main molecular layer interneurons with specific anatomical descriptions of their axon projections onto Purkinje cells.
summary: Mann-Metzer & Yarom (1999) describe basket and stellate cells as the predominant molecular layer interneurons, connected by weak electrical synapses that synchronise their activity. Basket cell axons wrap Purkinje cell somata in a basket-like structure; stellate axons terminate on Purkinje cell dendritic trees. Both receive excitatory input from parallel and climbing fibers.
quotes: There are three main types of inhibitory GABAergic interneurons: Golgi cells in the granular layer and the interneurons in the molecular layer, the basket and stellate cells.
Whereas the axons of basket cells create a basketlike structure around the Purkinje cell somata, stellate axons terminate on the dendritic trees of the Purkinje cells.
recording simultaneously from pairs of inhibitory neurons in the molecular layer, we show here that these interneurons are organized in local networks, interconnected by weak electrical synapses.

source_title: A deep-learning strategy to identify cell types across species from high-density extracellular recordings
node_relevance_reason: Directly identifies cerebellar cell types including Purkinje cells and molecular layer interneurons using electrophysiological signatures, providing functional characterisation.
summary: Beau et al. (2024) developed a deep-learning classifier for cell type identification from extracellular recordings, using the cerebellum as a testbed with ground-truth libraries for Purkinje cells, molecular layer interneurons, Golgi cells, and mossy fibers. The classifier achieves >95% accuracy and works across different cerebellar regions and species.
quotes: We combine optogenetic activation and pharmacology using the cerebellum as a testbed to generate a curated ground-truth library of electrophysiological properties for Purkinje cells, molecular layer interneurons, Golgi cells, and mossy fibers.

The classifier's predictions agree with expert classification on recordings using different probes, in different laboratories, from functionally distinct cerebellar regions, and across animal species.

source_title: Regulation of early cerebellar development
section: The ventricular zone and the origin of GABAergic cerebellar neurons
node_relevance_reason: Characterises the developmental origin of basket and stellate cells as inhibitory interneurons of the molecular layer born from ventricular zone progenitors, relevant to understanding the common progenitor of MLI subtypes.
summary: Lowenstein et al. (2022) reviews early cerebellar development, showing that basket and stellate cells (molecular layer interneurons) are born from ventricular zone progenitors at E16.5 through birth, after Lugaro and Golgi cells. Their specification requires Gsx1, Pax2, and Ascl1, and they migrate radially before settling in the molecular layer postnatally.
quotes: stellate and basket cells develop later (E16.5-birth), implying that cerebellar inhibitory neurons are generated in an inside-first/outside-after manner
The ablation of Ascl1 has been reported to severely impact the development of late born inhibitory interneurons, that is stellate and basket cells

source_title: Pinceau Organization in the Cerebellum Requires Distinct Functions of Neurofascin in Purkinje and Basket Neurons During Postnatal Development
section: Developmental organization of the cerebellar pinceau
node_relevance_reason: Characterises basket cells and Purkinje cells with specific markers (parvalbumin for both basket neurons and Purkinje neurons, calbindin as Purkinje-specific marker) relevant to node marker characterisation.
summary: Buttermore et al. (2012) demonstrates that parvalbumin (Parv) labels both Purkinje neurons and basket neurons in the molecular layer, while calbindin (Calb) is expressed specifically by Purkinje neurons and not basket neurons. Basket cell axons form pinceau synapses around Purkinje cell axon initial segments via Kv1.2 channels.
quotes: We performed immunostaining of wild-type cerebellar sections against parvalbumin (Parv) to label both Purkinje neurons and molecular layer interneurons, including basket neurons (Bastianelli, 2003). We also immunostained for Calb as a specific marker for Purkinje neurons
Parv expression in basket neurons (b) in the vicinity of the Purkinje neurons. Note that Parv is also expressed in Purkinje neurons, but Calb is not expressed in basket neurons.

source_title: Neurophysiology of the cerebellum and clinical correlations: a review
node_relevance_reason: Review characterising basket and stellate cells as inhibitory interneurons of the molecular layer targeting Purkinje cells, consistent with node anatomy but without specific marker evidence.
summary: Machado Filho et al. (2025) reviews cerebellar cytoarchitecture, confirming Purkinje cells as the largest neurons and primary site of damage in spinocerebellar ataxias. Basket and stellate cells in the molecular layer refine Purkinje cell output through somatic and dendritic inhibition respectively; Golgi cells modulate granular layer activity.
quotes: The molecular layer contains two main types of inhibitory interneurons, basket and stellate cells, as well as parallel fibers, which originate from granule cells.
basket and stellate cells refine Purkinje cell output through somatic and dendritic inhibition, respectively.

source_title: Tools for Cre-mediated conditional deletion of floxed alleles from developing cerebellar Purkinje cells
node_relevance_reason: Directly establishes Calb1 (calbindin) as a Purkinje-cell-specific marker through Cre-line characterisation, and describes basket cells and stellate cells as the molecular layer interneurons inhibiting Purkinje cells.
summary: Jahncke & Wright (2024) characterise multiple Cre lines for Purkinje cell targeting. A Calb1-Cre line drives efficient and complete recombination in embryonic Purkinje cells. They show that Ptf1a-Cre targets all GABAergic neurons including Purkinje cells and molecular layer interneurons (basket and stellate cells). Basket cells (purple) and stellate cells (blue) provide inhibitory input onto Purkinje cells from the molecular layer.
quotes: We identify a Calb1Cre line that drives efficient and complete recombination in embryonic Purkinje cells, resulting in loss of Dag1 protein before the period of synaptogenesis.
The molecular layer interneurons (basket cells, purple, and stellate cells, blue) provide inhibitory input onto Purkinje cells.

source_title: Anoctamin 2-chloride channels reduce simple spike activity and mediate inhibition at elevated calcium concentration in cerebellar Purkinje cells
node_relevance_reason: Characterises Purkinje cells with calbindin as marker (anti-Calbindin D-28K used in immunostaining) and describes molecular layer interneurons providing GABAergic inhibition onto Purkinje cells.
summary: Auer et al. (2021) confirms Ano2 mRNA expression in Purkinje cells and shows ANO2-mediated chloride currents attenuate Purkinje cell simple spike activity. Interneurons were identified by subtracting the calbindin signal from the parvalbumin signal (parvalbumin marks both Purkinje cells and MLIs; calbindin is Purkinje-specific), providing marker data for both cell types.
quotes: Interneurons were identified by subtracting the calbindin signal from the parvalbumin signal.
we report a reduction of inhibitory currents from GABAergic interneurons upon depolarization, lasting for several seconds.

source_title: Myocyte Enhancer Factor 2c Regulates Dendritic Complexity and Connectivity of Cerebellar Purkinje Cells
node_relevance_reason: Characterises Purkinje cells using calbindin and parvalbumin markers, with parvalbumin also labelling molecular layer interneurons (stellate/basket cells).
summary: Kamath & Chen (2019) show that Mef2c is specifically expressed in postnatal Purkinje cells (not stellate/basket cells or granule cells). Calbindin colocalises with Mef2c at P60 only in the Purkinje cell layer; parvalbumin labels both Purkinje cells and stellate/basket cells in the molecular layer.
quotes: At P60, Mef2c colocalizes with calbindin and parvalbumin in the Purkinje cell layer, but not parvalbumin in the molecular layer.
stellate/basket cells in the molecular layer and Purkinje cells in the Purkinje cell layer, whereas calbindin is expressed only by Purkinje cells

source_title: A transcriptomic atlas of the mouse cerebellum reveals regional specializations and novel cell types
node_relevance_reason: Key transcriptomic atlas that identifies MLI1 and MLI2 as two molecularly and functionally distinct types with continuous morphological variation, providing the primary source for Sorcs3/Nxph1 as MLI subtype markers.
summary: Kozareva et al. (2020/2021) produced the first comprehensive cerebellar transcriptomic atlas, finding that molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) comprise two molecularly and functionally distinct types (MLI1 and MLI2) with a continuum of morphological variation through the molecular layer. The two types differ in spontaneous firing, excitability, and electrical coupling, providing the primary evidence for MLI1/MLI2 distinction by Sorcs3 and Nxph1 expression.
quotes: most surprisingly, we found that molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) were composed of two molecularly and functionally distinct types.

Both show a continuum of morphological variation through the thickness of the molecular layer, but electrophysiological recordings revealed marked differences between the two types in spontaneous firing, excitability, and electrical coupling.

source_title: Developmental and evolutionary dynamics of cis-regulatory elements in mouse cerebellar cells
node_relevance_reason: Provides snATAC-seq atlas of mouse cerebellum including inhibitory interneurons (Purkinje cells, granule cells), relevant for regulatory landscape of MLI and Purkinje cell types.
summary: Sarropoulos et al. (2021) generated a single-cell atlas of gene regulation in the mouse cerebellum across 11 developmental stages using snATAC-seq (~90,000 cells). The study maps all major cerebellar cell types including Purkinje cells and inhibitory interneurons, showing gradual divergence of regulatory programs during differentiation and differences in CRE conservation between cell types.
quotes: By acquiring snATAC-seq profiles for ~90,000 cells spanning 11 stages, we mapped cerebellar cell types and identified candidate cis-regulatory elements (CREs).
Pleiotropic CREs in major cerebellar neuron types (granule cells, Purkinje cells, and inhibitory interneurons) are more active at early differentiation states.

source_title: Excitatory and inhibitory receptors utilize distinct post- and trans-synaptic mechanisms in vivo
node_relevance_reason: Characterises cerebellar molecular layer interneurons (MLIs) including lower MLIs (basket cells) targeting Purkinje cell somata and upper MLIs (stellate cells) targeting dendritic shafts, with parvalbumin (PV) as MLI marker.
summary: Miyazaki et al. (2021) used cell-autonomous elimination to study receptor localisation at cerebellar synapses. Lower MLIs (basket cells, PV-labeled) form pinceau synapses at Purkinje cell axon initial segments; upper MLIs (stellate cells) innervate dendritic shafts. GABAA receptors on Purkinje cells require inhibitory presynaptic terminals for their postsynaptic localisation.
quotes: lower MLIs or basket cells (ΔMLI), that is, PV-labeled somata in the lower ML VIAAT-labeled presynaptic terminals around PC somata, and PV/VIAAT-labeled pinceau formation at the base of PC somata
Upper MLIs corresponding to stellate cells innervate dendritic shafts of PCs.

source_title: Focusing on the Emerging Role of Kainate Receptors in the Dorsal Cochlear Nucleus (DCN) and Cerebellum
node_relevance_reason: Mentions cerebellar cell types including Purkinje cells, basket cells, stellate cells, and Golgi cells in the context of kainate receptor expression, but does not provide specific marker or functional evidence for the region nodes.
summary: Wu & Tang (2023) review kainate receptors in the cerebellum and the cerebellum-like dorsal cochlear nucleus. The five main cerebellar cell types are listed: Purkinje cells, granule cells, basket cells, stellate cells, and Golgi cells. All five except granule cells are inhibitory GABAergic neurons.
quotes: Purkinje cells, granule cells, basket cells, stellate cells, and Golgi cells are the five most significant cell types.
The major output of the cerebellar cortex is inhibitory because Purkinje cells project into the cells of the deep cerebellar nuclei

source_title: Genetic labeling reveals spatial and cellular expression pattern of neuregulin 1 in mouse brain
node_relevance_reason: Provides evidence that Nrg1 is expressed in cerebellar Purkinje cells (but not basket/stellate cells in the molecular layer), with parvalbumin (PV) as a Purkinje cell marker, relevant to Purkinje cell characterisation.
summary: Ding et al. (2023) show that Nrg1 is highly expressed in cerebellar Purkinje cells, identified by co-localisation with parvalbumin (PV). Nrg1 is absent from basket and stellate cells (GABAergic interneurons in the molecular layer identified by Gad67-GFP). Nrg1-expressing neurons in the Purkinje layer are PV-positive.
quotes: Nrg1 is highly expressed in the median eminence (ME) of hypothalamus and Purkinje cells in the cerebellum.
cell bodies and dendritic trees of Purkinje cells, indicated by the co-localization of tdTomato with parvalbumin (PV), a protein marker for Purkinje cells.

source_title: The Relationship Between Zebrin Expression and Cerebellar Functions: Insights From Neuroimaging Studies
node_relevance_reason: Characterises Purkinje cells with zebrin as a Purkinje-specific molecular marker, and mentions molecular layer GABAergic interneurons targeting Purkinje cell dendrites.
summary: Lin et al. (2020) review zebrin (aldolase C) as a Purkinje-cell-specific molecular marker that defines functional cerebellar zones. The molecular layer contains GABAergic inhibitory interneurons (basket and stellate cells) forming synapses onto Purkinje cell dendrites. Zebrin-positive Purkinje cells are resistant to excitotoxicity while zebrin-negative zones are more vulnerable.
quotes: zebrin stripe (a Purkinje cell-specific antibody molecular marker, which is a glycolytic enzyme expressed in cerebellar Purkinje cells)
The molecular layer contains GABAergic inhibitory interneurons that form synapses onto Purkinje cell dendrites.

source_title: Purkinje cell neurotransmission patterns cerebellar basket cells into zonal modules that are defined by distinct pinceau sizes
node_relevance_reason: Preprint of Zhou et al. 2020, characterising basket cell pinceau organisation in Purkinje cell zones using HCN1, Kv1.1, PSD95, GAD67 as basket cell pinceau markers.
summary: Zhou et al. 2020 bioRxiv preprint demonstrates that HCN1, Kv1.1, PSD95, and GAD67 mark patterns of basket cell pinceaux mapping onto Purkinje cell functional zones. Basket cells identified via Ascl1-CreERT2 show zone-specific pinceau sizes, and this patterning requires Purkinje cell neurotransmission.
quotes: HCN1, Kv1.1, PSD95 and GAD67 unexpectedly mark patterns of basket cell pinceaux that map onto Purkinje cell functional zones.
we reveal that basket cell zones comprise different sizes of pinceaux.
